analyst_view.overall: Early view: No. 3 St. Louis host No. 6 LAFC in Game 1; a draw after 90 minutes goes to penalties. St. Louis won the US Open Cup and set a 21-game unbeaten record under first-year coach Yoann Damet, but then lost four straight before a stoppage-time 1-0 win at Houston in which they were outshot 23-13. LAFC are under interim coach Xavi Tamarit after Marc Dos Santos left in late September, scored a club-low 52 league goals, went 3-7-7 on the road and are without Hugo Lloris, Aaron Long and Timothy Tillman.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.9 goals and I lean lower. LAFC scored the fewest league goals in their history and managed one goal from 24 shots at Seattle, while St. Louis had one shot on target at Houston and scored little during their four-game losing run. Denis Bouanga (18 goals) and Son Heung-min are the main threat, but a 1-0 or 1-1 fits better.

corners.text: The site expects 10.5 corners. I lean higher: LAFC won 12 corners at Seattle while dominating the ball, and St. Louis conceded nine to Houston on Decision Day while defending. If LAFC have long spells of possession again, the count should climb.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.9 cards. St. Louis committed 13 fouls at Houston without a booking, and Sergi Palencia, booked at Seattle, is listed by the site as banned; I could not confirm whether regular-season yellows carry into the playoffs. Nothing else points either way, so I stay with the number.

shots.text: The site expects 29.4 shots, with 17.1 for LAFC. I lean higher: LAFC took 24 at Seattle and Houston took 23 against St. Louis, so St. Louis are currently allowing a lot of attempts, and the hosts will have to push forward at home too.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.1 on target. LAFC put eight of 24 on goal at Seattle and St. Louis one of 13 at Houston, so volume is not turning into accuracy for either side; I stay close to the number despite expecting more shots.
